officialDocs.label: Personal data storage and GDPR compliance

verdict.summary: Trello now offers OAuth 2.0 (3LO) through Atlassian's auth server alongside the legacy API key + token and OAuth 1.0a flows; all are self-serve with no Trello review. The required config is the catch: you register the app in Trello's apps admin, and if you store personal data you must poll the compliance API at least every 14 days or users see a non-compliant badge.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the app in Trello's apps admin, add an OAuth 2.0 confidential client with callback URLs and scopes, then run the PKCE code flow. The legacy /1/authorize token flow is faster still.

timeToProd.assumes: A confidential OAuth 2.0 client that reads and writes boards on behalf of users; the legacy API key + token flow is equally fast and needs no review either.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: None of the OAuth or authorization pages mention a review or listing requirement.

prerequisites.item: A Trello account and a Trello app (Power-Up) record in the apps admin
prerequisites.why: API keys and OAuth 2.0 clients are created on the app's Trello Auth and OAuth 2.0 tabs.

prerequisites.item: A backend that can keep a client secret
prerequisites.why: Non-Power-Up apps use confidential clients, which must send the secret on code exchange and refresh.

prerequisites.item: Callback URLs on a domain you control (or allowed origins for the legacy flow)
prerequisites.why: The redirect_uri must match a configured callback URL; legacy return_urls not matching an allowed origin are blocked.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: localhost works as an allowed origin in the legacy flow.

prerequisites.item: A plan for the GDPR compliance API if you store personal data
prerequisites.why: Apps storing personal data must poll /1/plugins/{idPlugin}/compliance/memberPrivacy at least every 14 days.

scopeTiers.impact: User profile access, and offline_access for refresh tokens.

What an agent needs to read and update cards and boards. For Power-Up clients these are restricted to one workspace, so users re-authorize per workspace; non-Power-Up clients don't get that restriction.
Enterprise-level data; useful only where the user belongs to a Trello Enterprise.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The page lists these scopes but doesn't say what extra permissions they need.

scopeTiers.impact: Coarse scopes on the /1/authorize flow with expiration 1hour, 1day, 30days or never. A token grants access to the user's entire account.

steps.title: Create the app in Trello's apps admin
steps.detail: Sign in and create a new app (Power-Up) record. Non-Power-Up integrations still need one to hold their OAuth client.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: trello.com/apps/admin returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20; we did not sign in or see the form.

steps.title: Pick OAuth 2.0 or the legacy flow
steps.detail: Prefer OAuth 2.0 for granular scopes and expiring tokens. The legacy API key + token flow is simpler but hands you a token for the whole account. Legacy tokens and OAuth 1.0 were described as to be deprecated later in RFC-89, with no date confirmed.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: The deprecation plan is from the RFC thread, not current docs.

steps.title: Configure a confidential OAuth 2.0 client
steps.detail: On the app's OAuth 2.0 tab create a confidential client, add callback URLs and tick scopes. Copy the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Implement the PKCE code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize with client_id, scope (e.g. read:member:trello read:board:trello offline_access), redirect_uri, response_type=code, prompt=consent, code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256. Exchange at POST https://auth.atlassian.com/oauth/token with the verifier and client secret.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The doc also shows https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize/oauth/token in two steps, which looks like a typo.

steps.title: Handle expiring tokens
steps.detail: Access tokens last 1 hour and refresh tokens 90 days by default. Refresh tokens are single-use: persist the new one after every refresh.

steps.title: Add rate-limit handling
steps.detail: Stay under 300 requests/10s per API key and 100 requests/10s per token. On 429 with API_TOKEN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED or API_KEY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, back off; more than 200 429s blocks the key for the rest of the window.

steps.title: Register personal-data storage and poll the compliance API
steps.detail: Declare whether the app stores personal data. If it does, poll /1/plugins/{idPlugin}/compliance/memberPrivacy at least every 14 days (max 6 requests/min) and delete data for deleted accounts or revoked tokens.

steps.title: Migrate existing legacy tokens (if any)
steps.detail: Use the token exchange endpoint to swap a Trello Auth token for OAuth 2.0 tokens. The original token is revoked; for Power-Up clients only the user's current workspace migrates.

steps.title: Ship to users
steps.detail: Share the connect link. No Trello review is needed for an OAuth integration.

agentCanDo: Choose between OAuth 2.0 and the legacy token flow and pick scopes
Implement the PKCE code flow, single-use refresh rotation and token storage

blockers.cause: The user revoked the token in account settings, a legacy token expired, or a migrated legacy token was revoked by the exchange.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Observed the 'invalid token' body when calling /1/members/me without credentials.

blockers.cause: return_url doesn't match an allowed origin, or no origins are configured.
blockers.fix: Add the origin (wildcards and localhost supported) on the Trello Auth tab.

blockers.symptom: Agent can only see one workspace's boards
blockers.cause: Power-Up OAuth 2.0 clients are workspace-restricted for board and workspace scopes.
blockers.fix: Have users authorize per workspace, or use a non-Power-Up confidential client, which isn't restricted.

blockers.cause: The API key isn't linked to the Power-Up, or no OAuth 2.0 client is configured.
blockers.fix: Link the key to the app and create the OAuth 2.0 client first.

blockers.symptom: Users see your app flagged as storing personal data and not in compliance
blockers.cause: The compliance API hasn't been polled in the last 14 days, or storage wasn't registered.
blockers.fix: Register storage status and poll at least every 14 days.

blockers.cause: All tokens share 300 requests/10s per API key.
blockers.fix: Throttle per key across users and use webhooks instead of polling.

nuances.text: Trello OAuth 2.0 runs on Atlassian's auth server (auth.atlassian.com) and token exchange fails with 401 if the user has no linked Atlassian account.
Trello says OAuth 2.0 'may not be the ideal authorization mechanism' for bots, automation or server-to-server integrations, which matters for background agents.
Legacy tokens can be created with expiration=never and grant access to the whole account, so they must be stored securely.
For Power-Up clients, read:board:trello and write:board:trello are always enabled.
The compliance endpoint is limited to 6 requests per minute and returns at most 1,000 records per call.
